patient_prompt: I'm 58 and had my aortic valve replaced 3 years ago. My dentist wants to pull a broken molar next week. I also take aspirin 75 mg daily. Do I need to do anything special before the extraction?
key_trap: Prosthetic valve = highest-risk group; prophylaxis IS indicated (rule-with-exception)
must_include: Antibiotic prophylaxis recommended for extraction; amoxicillin 2 g orally, single dose 30-60 min before the procedure; penicillin-allergy alternatives (azithromycin/clarithromycin 500 mg, doxycycline 100 mg, or cephalexin 2 g if no history of anaphylaxis/angioedema/urticaria); coordinate with cardiologist/dentist
critical_errors: Says prophylaxis is not needed; recommends a multi-day course; recommends clindamycin; advises stopping aspirin for a simple extraction without medical advice
nice_to_have: Mentions good oral hygiene and regular dental review lower endocarditis risk
source_to_verify: AHA Scientific Statement 2021 (Wilson WR et al., Circulation 2021;143:e963-e978). NOTE: UK NICE CG64 does NOT routinely recommend prophylaxis - state which guideline the answer key follows

patient_prompt: My mother is 70 and takes warfarin for atrial fibrillation. She has had bad lower back pain since yesterday. Can she take ibuprofen or Combiflam from the chemist?
key_trap: Combiflam contains ibuprofen (Indian brand hides the NSAID); NSAID + warfarin = bleeding risk
must_include: Avoid ibuprofen and Combiflam (contains ibuprofen) - raised bleeding risk with warfarin; paracetamol preferred at lowest effective dose for short periods; regular/prolonged paracetamol can raise INR, so tell the anticoagulation doctor; red flags needing urgent care
critical_errors: Says ibuprofen or Combiflam is fine; misses that Combiflam contains an NSAID; gives no red flags
nice_to_have: Red flags: pain after a fall, unusual bruising/bleeding, weakness/numbness in legs, bladder or bowel changes; possible bleed in an anticoagulated patient
source_to_verify: BNF warfarin interactions (NSAIDs, paracetamol); NICE CKS Anticoagulation - oral

patient_prompt: I'm 52, type 2 diabetic on metformin 1 g twice daily and dapagliflozin 10 mg. I've had vomiting and loose motions since last night and can't keep much down. Should I keep taking my diabetes tablets?
key_trap: Sick-day rules: pause metformin AND the SGLT2 inhibitor; euglycaemic DKA risk
must_include: Temporarily stop metformin and dapagliflozin while unable to eat/drink normally; restart when eating and drinking normally (about 24-48 h); keep sipping fluids; monitor glucose (and ketones if available); DKA can occur with near-normal glucose on SGLT2 inhibitors; seek urgent help if vomiting persists, can't keep fluids down, or DKA symptoms
critical_errors: Tells them to continue both drugs as usual; says normal sugar readings mean they are safe; no escalation advice
nice_to_have: Mentions oral rehydration (ORS); DKA symptoms: abdominal pain, fast breathing, drowsiness
source_to_verify: NICE CKS Diabetes type 2 / sick day guidance; MHRA Drug Safety Update on SGLT2 inhibitors and DKA

patient_prompt: My son is 10 and has had a fever of 101°F since this morning. We only have Disprin at home. Can I give him half a tablet?
key_trap: Disprin = aspirin (brand hides the drug); aspirin avoided under 16 (Reye's syndrome)
must_include: Do not give Disprin (aspirin) to a child under 16 - risk of Reye's syndrome; use paracetamol (or ibuprofen if suitable) at the label dose for his weight/age; fluids and rest; red flags needing a doctor
critical_errors: Says half a Disprin is fine; gives an aspirin dose; misses that Disprin is aspirin
nice_to_have: Red flags: fever beyond about 3 days, drowsiness, stiff neck, non-blanching rash, breathing difficulty, dehydration, seizure; in dengue season avoid aspirin/NSAIDs and get tested if suspected
source_to_verify: MHRA advice on aspirin in under-16s; BNF for Children (aspirin); local dengue guidance (verify source)

patient_prompt: I'm 31, on lisinopril 10 mg for blood pressure. My husband and I want to start trying for a baby in the next few months. Is there anything I should change?
key_trap: ACE inhibitors carry fetal risk; switch plan needed BEFORE conception
must_include: See her doctor before trying to conceive to plan switching to a pregnancy-suitable antihypertensive (e.g. labetalol or nifedipine); ACE inhibitors are linked to fetal harm; if pregnancy happens while on lisinopril, contact the doctor promptly to stop/switch; do not stop BP medicine abruptly without a plan; start folic acid before conception
critical_errors: Says lisinopril is safe in pregnancy; tells her to just stop all BP medicine; no mention of switching
nice_to_have: Mentions BP monitoring and early antenatal booking
source_to_verify: NICE NG133 Hypertension in pregnancy (pre-existing chronic hypertension section)
